2. Requirements
2.1 The Bank requires that Borrowers (including beneficiaries of Bank financing); bidders
(applicants/proposers), consultants, contractors and suppliers; any sub-contractors,
sub-consultants, service providers or suppliers; any agents (whether declared or not);
and any of their personnel, observe the highest standard of ethics during the
procurement process, selection and contract execution of Bank-financed contracts, and
refrain from Fraud and Corruption.
2.2 To this end, the Bank:
a. Defines, for the purposes of this provision, the terms set forth below as follows:
i. “corrupt practice” is the offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting, directly or
indirectly, of anything of value to influence improperly the actions of another
party;
ii. “fraudulent practice” is any act or omission, including misrepresentation, that
knowingly or recklessly misleads, or attempts to mislead, a party to obtain
financial or other benefit or to avoid an obligation;
iii. “collusive practice” is an arrangement between two or more parties designed to
achieve an improper purpose, including to influence improperly the actions of
another party;
iv. “coercive practice” is impairing or harming, or threatening to impair or harm,
directly or indirectly, any party or the property of the party to influence
improperly the actions of a party;
v. “obstructive practice” is:
(a) deliberately destroying, falsifying, altering, or concealing of evidence
material to the investigation or making false statements to investigators
in order to materially impede a Bank investigation into allegations of a
corrupt, fraudulent, coercive, or collusive practice; and/or threatening,
harassing, or intimidating any party to prevent it from disclosing its
knowledge of matters relevant to the investigation or from pursuing the
investigation; or
(b) acts intended to materially impede the exercise of the Bank’s inspection
and audit rights provided for under paragraph 2.2 e. below.
b. Rejects a proposal for award if the Bank determines that the firm or individual
recommended for award, any of its personnel, or its agents, or its sub-consultants,
sub-contractors, service providers, suppliers and/ or their employees, has, directly or
indirectly, engaged in corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive, or obstructive practices
in competing for the contract in question;
c. In addition to the legal remedies set out in the relevant Legal Agreement, may take
other appropriate actions, including declaring misprocurement, if the Bank
determines at any time that representatives of the Borrower or of a recipient of any
part of the proceeds of the loan engaged in corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive, or
obstructive practices during the procurement process, selection and/or execution of
the contract in question, without the Borrower having taken timely and appropriate
action satisfactory to the Bank to address such practices when they occur, including
by failing to inform the Bank in a timely manner at the time they knew of the
practices;
d. Pursuant to the Bank’s Anti-Corruption Guidelines, and in accordance with the Bank’s
prevailing sanctions policies and procedures, may sanction a firm or individual, either
indefinitely or for a stated period of time, including by publicly declaring such firm or
individual ineligible (i) to be awarded or otherwise benefit from a Bank-financed
contract, financially or in any other manner;1 (ii) to be a nominated2 sub-contractor,
consultant, manufacturer or supplier, or service provider of an otherwise eligible firm
being awarded a Bank-financed contract; and (iii) to receive the proceeds of any loan
made by the Bank or otherwise to participate further in the preparation or
implementation of any Bank-financed project;
e. Requires that a clause be included in bidding/request for proposals documents and
in contracts financed by a Bank loan, requiring (i) bidders (applicants/proposers),
consultants, contractors, and suppliers, and their sub-contractors, sub-consultants,
service providers, suppliers, agents, personnel, permit the Bank to inspect3 all
accounts, records and other documents relating to the procurement process,
For the avoidance of doubt, a sanctioned party’s ineligibility to be awarded a contract shall include, without limitation, (i)
applying for pre-qualification, expressing interest in a consultancy, and bidding, either directly or as a nominated sub-
contractor, nominated consultant, nominated manufacturer or supplier, or nominated service provider, in respect of such
contract, and (ii) entering into an addendum or amendment introducing a material modification to any existing contract.
A nominated sub-contractor, nominated consultant, nominated manufacturer or supplier, or nominated service provider
(different names are used depending on the particular bidding document) is one which has been: (i) included by the bidder in
its pre-qualification application or bid because it brings specific and critical experience and know-how that allow the bidder

Inspections in this context usually are investigative (i.e., forensic) in nature. They involve fact-finding activities undertaken

rows.section: Section VII - Requirements of the Information System
rows.description:
Legal and Regulatory Requirements to be met by the Information
System
The Pakistan Regulatory Registry (PRR) is a national government platform that consolidates,
governs, and publishes regulatory obligations applicable on businesses across federal and all
provincial jurisdictions. Given its mandate to serve as the authoritative national repository of
RLCOs i.e. RLCO” means any rules, licenses, circulars, orders, regulations, SROs, by-laws,
notifications, certificates, office memoranda, permits, instructions, forms, authorizations,
directives, resolution or other instruments made, issued or enforced by a Government Agency
with regulatory effect and functions, and includes such other instruments as may be notified
by the Federal Government, the Information System and its implementation must comply with
all applicable laws, regulations, government policies, and international standards referenced in
this sub-section. Compliance with these requirements is mandatory throughout the design,
development, deployment, and operational life of the System.

The PRR Information System MUST support two co-equal and inseparable workstreams: (i)
the PRR Platform - a national multi-jurisdictional digital platform comprising ten mandatory
functional modules; and (ii) the Technical Assistance (TA) Workstream - a structured
programme of regulatory mapping, capacity building, workflow documentation, and reform
facilitation that operationalises the PRR and drives measurable reform outcomes. The business
function requirements for each workstream are set out below. Compliance with all
requirements in this sub-section is mandatory. Where a module is designated as a separately
priced subsystem, the Supplier MUST price it as a distinct line item in the System Inventory
Tables and Implementation Schedule; this designation does not render the module optional.

rows.section: Section VII - Requirements of the Information System
rows.description:
Architectural Requirements to be met by the Information System
The PRR Information System MUST be built as a multi-layered, modular, and service-oriented
platform - not a single monolithic application. The architecture MUST support the full
breadth of the PRR's mandate: registry operations, legal metadata governance, workflow
orchestration, public access and consultation, BPR and reform analytics, RIS gatekeeping, AI-
assisted diagnostics, and management dashboards - across six jurisdictions simultaneously.
The architecture described in this sub-section is the reference architecture. Proposers may
propose an alternative architecture provided they demonstrate that it meets or exceeds all
requirements set out in this sub-section and throughout Section VII.
Security and Ownership Controls: The System MUST enforce strong RBAC and agency
scoping for all draft and internal records. All mapping actions MUST be captured in
immutable audit logs. Government ownership and control of all data, configurations, and
artifacts MUST be maintained at all times, with no vendor lock-in.
Proposed overall architecture requirements have been illustrated at Figure-16

Systems Administration and Management Functions Required to
be met by the Information System
The Information System MUST provide comprehensive administration, monitoring, and
management capabilities that allow BOI/AKTU administrators to govern the platform, manage
users, configure system behaviour, maintain security, and monitor operational health - all
without vendor involvement in routine administrative tasks. An Administration Portal MUST
be provided as a dedicated, secured interface for these functions, accessible only to authorised
administrators with mandatory multi-factor authentication enforced at all times.

The Information System MUST achieve and sustain the performance levels specified in this

surges, mapping campaigns, or bulk ingestion operations. The Supplier MUST conduct and
document load testing and performance benchmarking prior to each Operational Acceptance
Test, using test scenarios that reflect the concurrent user and transaction volumes specified
below.

rows.description:
Cyber Security Requirements
The Information System MUST be designed, developed, and operated with security embedded
at every layer of the architecture - from the public portal through the government portals,
workflow services, data stores, and integration points. Security is a foundational requirement
of the PRR, not an afterthought. The System carries Official Government Data as defined in
sub-section 1.3.3.4, and MUST meet all applicable Pakistani laws, GoP security standards, and
international benchmarks specified in this sub-section. Compliance with GoP cybersecurity
standards is a mandatory pre-condition for the issuance of the Operational Acceptance
Certificate.

ADDENDUM TO SECTION B - SUPPLEMENTARY ARCHITECTURAL
PRINCIPLES
The following supplementary architectural principles from the Purchaser's original technical
requirements are provided as additional mandatory context to the architectural requirements in
sub-section 1.3. They elaborate the design intent and performance philosophy that underpins
the minimum requirements specified in sub-sections 1.3.1 through 1.3.6.
AP-1 High Availability and National-Scale Performance
The PRR architecture MUST support millions of public read transactions, batch uploads from
departments, high concurrent consultation submissions, and horizontal scalability via container
orchestration. Public read performance and secure write integrity MUST be balanced by
separating read-optimised infrastructure (CDN, search cluster, caching) from write-path
services (RLCO submission, workflow engine, review console).
AP-2 Cloud-Agnostic and Sovereign Deployment
The System MUST deploy on Government of Pakistan infrastructure - private data centre or
approved public cloud. Containerisation (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes or equivalent)
are mandatory. The System MUST avoid proprietary vendor lock-in and MUST comply with
national data residency requirements. Digital sovereignty is non-negotiable.
AP-3 Security and Privacy by Design
Security MUST be embedded at every layer of the architecture. This requires RBAC with least-
privilege, mandatory MFA for government users, encryption at rest and in transit, API
throttling and abuse prevention, and vulnerability scanning and code audits throughout the
development and operational lifecycle. PSS compliance is a mandatory pre-condition for
Operational Acceptance. The Supplier MUST provide a PSS Compliance Matrix as a
mandatory deliverable. A four-tier data classification MUST be applied to every field in the
RLCO data model: (1) Public - published on portal; (2) Government Restricted - agencies
only; (3) Internal - BOI/AKTU only; (4) Confidential - encrypted at rest, HSM-protected.
AP-4 Search-Optimised and Discoverable Architecture
Regulatory information MUST be easily discoverable. The architecture MUST implement full-
text indexed search (OpenSearch or Elasticsearch), filters by sector, authority, jurisdiction, and
instrument type, saved searches and alert subscriptions, and economic activity-based
compliance views. If businesses cannot find it, it does not exist as effective regulation.
AP-5 Version-Controlled and Time-Aware Design
The System MUST support effective date tracking for all RLCOs, historical snapshot retrieval,
future-dated regulatory changes, and automatic deactivation of RLCOs upon expiry.
Regulatory time-state MUST be machine-readable and queryable.
AP-6 Multilingual and Inclusive Architecture
The System MUST implement full RTL support for Urdu, multilingual interface and content
governance workflows, WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility compliance, locale-aware date and
number formatting, Unicode NFC normalisation, Jameel Noori Nastaleeq or equivalent web-
safe Urdu font, CSS 'direction: rtl' with bidirectional support, and a Urdu language analyser
integrated in the search index. Inclusivity is a structural, not a cosmetic, requirement.
AP-7 Data Integrity and Validation Controls
Built-in validation rules MUST prevent duplicate RLCO entries, orphaned references, missing
legal citations, and invalid metadata combinations. Validation MUST be systemic and
automated - not dependent on manual review. The PRR template validation engine, as
specified in sub-section 1.2.1.1, is the primary implementation mechanism.
AP-8 Observability and Proactive Monitoring
The System MUST provide centralised logging across all services, real-time dashboards
showing RLCO coverage percentage, pending reviews, and consultation cycles, automated
alerting for abnormal patterns, and continuous system health monitoring. Operational
resilience MUST be measurable and reported monthly to the Purchaser.
AP-9 Extensibility for Reform and Analytics
The architecture MUST enable regulatory burden measurement using the SCM methodology,
regulatory impact assessment analytics, B-READY and SMART reform tracking, and sector-
wise compliance time and cost analysis. The PRR must evolve into a reform intelligence engine
- not merely a regulatory document repository. Reform analytics capabilities are mandatory,
not optional features.
